title: Subtoken latency sentinels & geo-failover orchestration: dashboard build and runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a compact, operational dashboard and accompanying runbook that surfaces subtoken-level latency regressions and ties them to multi-region failover events and circuit-breaker activations. The aim is to give on-call engineers one pane to: 1) quickly determine whether high tail latency is a decoding/subtoken phenomenon, batching artifact, or cross-region spillback; 2) see which circuit(s) tripped and which tenants/routes are being shed; 3) trigger well-defined mitigations (regional fencing, model fallback, scaled shedding) and validate impact.

Scope:
- Instrumentation schema for 'subtoken' timings (tokenization -> model input, generation per subtoken, kv cache hit/miss attribution).
- New SLI derivations: subtoken-p50/p95/p99 and subtoken-emit-rate normalized per-request; kv-cache-hit-rate correlated with latency percentiles.
- Annotations for region-failover events and circuit-breaker state transitions in the dashboard.
- A lightweight runbook (on-call checklist + automated remediation snippets) and crisis telegraph (Slack / Pager duty playbook).
- Backfill historical 90-day heatmap for baseline detection and anomaly-trigger thresholds.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Subtoken vs token: we chose the finer-grained 'subtoken' timing to capture glue code and tokenizer regressions which often show up at subtoken boundaries; it increases metric cardinality but gives earlier signal. We will only capture per-request aggregated histograms and sampled per-subtoken traces (1/1000 requests) to control ingestion costs.
- Retention vs observability: keep full subtoken histograms for 30 days, 90-day rollups as quantile sketches.
- Circuit annotations: instead of duplicating circuit state per-metric, annotate timeline events and surface last-activation cause (e.g., 'p99-surge-shard-12') to reduce series explosion.

Telemetry schema (high-level):
- metric.name: infra.subtoken.latency_ms (labels: region, shard, model_family, route, tenant_tier, kv_hit boolean)
- metric.name: infra.subtoken.kv_hit_rate (labels: region, shard, model_family)
- events: infra.circuit.state_change (payload annotated into dashboard)
- trace sampling: subtoken-trace/{request_id} (1:1000) with referential link to logs and decode traces.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before rollout):
- Grafana dashboard implemented with: 1) per-region subtoken p99 heatmap, 2) time-aligned circuit state band, 3) tenant impact panel showing top-10 affected tenants and request-rate reduction from shedding.
- Alerting: automated PagerDuty trigger when region-p99-subtoken > 2x baseline for 5m AND tenant-shed-rate > 5% for same window.
- Runbook published with step-by-step mitigation (regional fence, model fallback, temporary quota bump) and playbook test completed in staging (simulated failover).
- Cost guardrails in place: sampling rate switchable via feature-flag; rolling back sampling to 0.1% within 15m if ingestion rises unexpectedly.

Workplan / tasks left:
- (ENG) Implement subtoken histogram aggregation in request-collector (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/collector/pull/482).
- (ENG) Add KV-cache label propagation and event annotation pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/event-annotator/pull/77).
- (SRE) Compose dashboard panels + derive alert thresholds from 90d baseline.
- (SRE) Create runbook + automate Slack escalation snippets.
- (QA) Run staging failover drill and validate signal fidelity.

Risks / mitigations:
- Metric cardinality growth: mitigated by restricting high-cardinal labels to p95/p99 rollups only; sampling for traces.
- False positives during bursty deployments: use deploy-window suppression and require amplitude + duration conditions for PagerDuty.
- Regulatory sensitivity: subtoken traces avoid logging PII; security review required.

Notes: this ticket intentionally focuses on observability and operational playbook; separate follow-ups will implement automated regional fencing or auto-fallback logic once confidence in signals is established.
